headline: Approved design plans for the El Centro project at Peabody Street Park, with a return visit before final designs are done.
summary: The commission also approved four event and site requests, including a Halloween drone show at Furlong Park. Katelyn Holappa said residents generally opposed a nine or ten space parking lot on the Furlong Park parcel and want green space.
decisions: Approved the August 18, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Approved use of the Salem Common Bandstand for Mayors Night Out on September 25, 2026, unanimously.
Approved a Community Message Board on the Common, pending a walk through with Trish or Joe, unanimously.
Approved use of the Salem Common Gazebo for a wedding on July 17, 2027, unanimously.
Approved use of the Furlong Park baseball field for a Halloween Night drone show on October 31, 2026, unanimously.
Approved moving forward with design plans for the El Centro project at Peabody Street Park, on the condition that they return before final designs are done, unanimously.

MINUTES OF THE SALEM PARK AND RECREATION COMMISSION 
SEPTEMBER 15, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Parks and Recreation Commission was held on September 15, 2026, at 6:45 p.m. 
at 401 Bridge Street.  Present were Chair James Shea; Members: Deborah Amaral and Bob Callahan; 
Trish O’Brien, Superintendent and Commission Clerk Joanne Roomey. Absent was Amy Everitt and 
Alex Sanchez.  
 
James Shea, Chairman called the meeting to order at 6:45 p.m. 
1. Approval of Park and Recreation Commission Minutes of August 18, 2026.   
Mr. Callahan made  a motion to approve the Park and Recreation Commission Minutes of 
August 18, 2026.  Ms. Amaral seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously. 
2. Visitors and Requests: 
a. Jordan Santiago appeared on behalf of the Salem Common Neighborhood Association for 
approval to have Mayors Night Out at the Salem Common Bandstand  on September 25, 
2026. Amplification from 5:30pm -9:00pm. They will also be showing a family friendly 
movie.  
There being no further questions or comments regarding this matter. Mr. Callahan made a 
motion to approve the use of the Salem Common Bandstand.  Ms. Amaral seconded the motion.  
The motion carried unanimously. 
b. Milo Martinez appeared on behalf of the  Salem Common Neighborhood Association  for 
approval to install a Community Message Board on the Common, which has already been 
approved by the Historic Commission. The proposed board will measure approximately 30" 
x 30" and provide space for up to nine sheets of paper for community advertisements and 
notices. 
Milo indicated that the proposed location is near the pillars on the Common. Mr. Callahan asked 
whether the area was gated. Trish expressed concern that the board does not interfere with the 
area used by Jeremy for food trucks. Milo reviewed the diagram included with the application
2 
 
and explained the proposed location. He indicated that he is willing to relocate the board if 
necessary and noted that the gate may need to be opened to access the area. 
The Commission discussed positioning the board parallel to the pathways between the pillars 
and agreed that it should not block the gate. Bob suggested moving it slightly to the right of the 
pillar. Milo asked if someone could accompany him to determine the most appropriate location, 
and the commission said Joe Candelaria could assist. 
Trish asked why the board would not want it to be placed outside the main entrance to the 
Common. Milo explained that they would prefer a location closer to the playground, where the 
information would be more accessible to and geared toward residents. Milo stated that someone 
will monitor the board from the Neighborhood Association and that contact information will 
be provided. 
Milo made two additional suggestions: 
1. A preacher had been present on the Common and was using a microphone. It was noted 
that a permit may be required for amplified sound, and the Police Department had been 
contacted regarding the matter.  
 
2. Regarding the markers used to mark the walking path, a suggestion was made for folks to 
consider using flags or marking the grass with temporary spray rather than the current 
markers. 
 
There being no further questions or comments regarding this matter.  Mr. Callahan made a 
motion to approve the use of the Community Message Board on the Common. Pending a walk 
through with Trish or Joe.  Ms. Amaral seconded the motion.  The motion carried unanimously. 
c. Danielle Aviles appeared for approval to have their wedding at Salem Common Gazebo on 
July 17, 2027. Amplification from 4:00 -5:00pm. They estimate 125 attendees. Hamilton 
Hall will be handling it. They will set up and take down everything. 
There being no further questions or comments regarding this matter.   Mr. Callahan made a 
motion to approve the use of the Salem Common Gazebo.  Ms. Amaral seconded the motion.  
The motion carried unanimously. 
d. Bonner Family, Birthday party, Pickman Park, October 10, 2026. Amplification from 
11:00am-1:00pm. Bounce house requested. Did not appear 
e. Jeremy Fiske appeared on behalf of the City of Salem  for approval for Halloween Night 
Drone Show at Furlong Park baseball field  on October 31, 2026.  Also celebrating Salem 
400. He stated that the set up for the event is planned to take place for most of the day.  
Jeremy discussed the drone show that will be part of the event. At the conclusion of the drone 
show, an arrow will be displayed directing attendees toward the train station for departure. 
The Commission asked about potential safety concerns related to the drone show. Jeremy 
explained that the drone operation will comply with  all applicable rules and regulations. The 
drones will be flown over the river, and the operation will be coordinated with the Police 
Department.
3 
 
There being no further questions or comments regarding this matter. Mr. Callahan made a 
motion to approve the use of Furlong Park baseball field .  Ms. Amaral seconded the motion.  
The motion carried unanimously. 
f. Jonathan Evans and Terese  Graf appeared on behalf of MASS Design Group and presented 
the proposed El Centro project at Peabody Street Park. Th ey provided background on the 
project and discussed the site restrictions associated with contaminated soils. 
They discussed the proposed play structures and  acknowledged the site and design 
considerations associated with the structures. 
The presentation incorporated feedback received at the July 21 meeting, including requests 
to incorporate a water component and to clarify and enhance the areas designated for play. 
The overall goal is to create a multigenerational space serving young children, teens, adults, 
and seniors, while creating a gateway to the area and celebrating the South River. The proposed 
design includes two play zones, a central gathering zone, an amph itheater, and water -play 
elements. 
There being no further questions or comments regarding this matter. Mr. Callahan made a 
motion to approve to move forward with the design plans for the El Centro project for Peabody 
Street Park on the condition that they come back again before the final designs are done.  Ms. 
Amaral seconded the motion.  The motion carried unanimously. 
3. Old Business: N/A 
4. New Business:  
Katelyn Holappa appeared before the Commission regarding the Furlong Park parcel adjacent to the 
park and discussed potential community uses and benefits for the property. 
Katelyn explained that she had met with City staff, the Mayor, Trish O’Brien, James Shea, Beth 
Rennard, and James Wellock regarding the parcel and was asked to obtain feedback from 
constituents. She acknowledged that there had been concerns among neighboring residents and said 
that the goal was to bring the community together and rebuild trust with residents and the builder. 
A community meeting was held the previous week, with approximately  20 to 30 residents. Katelyn 
said that residents were generally opposed to the proposal to create a nine or ten space parking lot on 
the parcel. Instead, residents wanted to use the property as a green space and have continued 
community input regarding its future use. 
Katelyn also said that the anticipated timeline for beginning work was approximately one year and 
that residents were interested in remaining involved with the developers throughout the process. 
The Commission discussed the history of the proposed parking lot. Bob asked why a parking lot was being 
considered, noting that his understanding was that the developer would clean up and maintain the land. It was 
explained that the Commission had previously discussed the parking lot with Mr. Trainois, who had offered 
to construct approximately nine parking spaces.
4 
 
Katelyn explained that, based on her discussions with Mr. Trainois, his interest in the parking spaces was to 
provide visitor parking for the condominium development . Commissioners questioned whether nine or ten 
spaces would have a meaningful impact and noted that the Commission would need to regulate any parking 
arrangement. 
Bob recalled that the original discussion involved the city receiving the entire parking lot, with  
Mr. Trainois initially proposing to construct nine spaces, and the city agreeing to accept them. Trish 
recalled that the initial discussion also involved providing parking for Little League games. She said 
that neighbors had indicated that they did not want a permanent parking lot but did not object to 
people parking on the property during Little League games. Residents expressed a preference for 
green space. 
Katelyn explained that the city owns Parcel A, including approximately 17 feet of the area, while the 
developer owns the adjoining 17 feet. She stated that the city currently has possession of the entire 
parcel and that Mr. Trainois had expressed an interest in acquiring a portion of it. 
Katelyn further explained that if a parking lot is not constructed, Mr. Trainois has proposed 
connecting the path behind the baseball park. She s aid that residents liked that idea and that the 
community preferred green space rather than a parking lot. The possibility of creating a larger loop 
around the waterfront and connecting the path to the river was also discussed. 
Jacob St. Louis, a neighbor, spoke in support of maintaining some type of green space, including 
trees. He explained that the initial  discussion had centered on whether the city should proceed with 
a land swap and what the property could be used for. 
5. Adjournment: There being no further business to come before the Salem Park and R ecreation 
Commission this evening. Mr. Callahan moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Ms. Amaral. 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:50 p.m.   
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Joanne M. Roomey 
Commission Clerk
